raw_response:
I farm 6 mu, and with wheat-maize on the same land, I will run the full 6 mu through winter wheat first and then summer maize after harvest. I have done this a long time, so I do not start from zero. I start from what usually works here in southern Hebei and then I trim or add a little based on water, money, and how hard I want to push yield. Since I have well irrigation, I will not save too much on water, because if wheat misses water at jointing or filling, or maize misses water around tasseling, the yield drops fast and that loss hurts more than a bit of extra cost. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, rotary till after maize, put most phosphorus and potassium in as base fertilizer, and split nitrogen between base and spring topdressing. I will aim around 650 kg per mu, not chase the very highest number, because I am farming alone and I need a plan I can actually manage. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed, mostly no-till into the wheat stubble to save labor and catch the season on time. I will put some fertilizer with sowing and the rest of the nitrogen at the big flare stage. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than watch the stand go pale and lose ears. Around here, if neighbors are feeding wheat and maize properly and I go light, I will be the one losing money at harvest. So this year I will keep inputs steady, use water at the key times, and hold the line on weeds, aphids, rust, and corn borers.
